disagreements.topic: Size of the haircut to FY28 consensus EPS ($23.85)
disagreements.positions: agent_2 -1.5% ($23.5), agent_5 -6% ($22.5), agent_1 and agent_4 -8% ($22.0), agent_3 -10% ($21.5). Agents 1, 3 and 4 justify the larger haircut the same way: consensus FY28 revenue is +20% while SEMI's July forecast has 2028 WFE only +14.1% (~$200B).
disagreements.resolution: That reason is out of date. At SEMICON Taiwan (Sept 1, 2026) SEMI's Clark Tseng raised the 2028 WFE forecast to $220B from ~$200B in July. On an unchanged ~$175B 2027 base, that is ~+25% for 2028, in line with or above consensus revenue +20%. The Sept-29 consensus probably already reflects this, so it is not upside to consensus. But it removes the stated case for an 8-10% haircut. A generic late-cycle haircut of ~4-5% (NTM EPS ~$22.8) is still reasonable. agent_5 was the only one to find and use the September upgrade.
disagreements.evidence: Digitimes 2026-09-01 (SEMI senior director Clark Tseng at SEMICON Taiwan: 2028 WFE raised to $220B from ~$200B); SEMI July 14 mid-year release (Yahoo Finance syndication: WFE +21.8% in 2027 and +14.1% in 2028 to ~$200B).

disagreements.positions: Fair values have converged to $505-515 (mean $511.4). Multiples: 21-23.5x on NTM EPS, with ~$8/share net cash in every model (a partial discount of the equity stakes; the 10-Q gives $10.0/share in full, $7.0 excluding them).
disagreements.resolution: There is no factual dispute left. The spread in fair value comes from the EPS haircut, not the multiple. With NTM EPS ~$22.8 x 22.5x + $10.0 net cash (10-Q), I get ~$523. Caveat: all five adopted the round-1 supervisor's net cash, consensus and multiple band, so their agreement is not five independent confirmations.
disagreements.evidence: Agents' round-2 fair_value.methods; MarketScreener consensus (via round 1). Q3 FY26 10-Q balance sheet (net cash $7,957M, 793.6M shares).

disagreements.topic: BIS Affiliates Rule / US-China truce date
disagreements.positions: All five now list 2027-01-10. agents 2 and 5 call the extension a single secondary report. agent_4 adds Fibre2Fashion.
disagreements.resolution: The truce extension to Jan 10, 2027 was announced by Treasury Secretary Bessent on Sep 23 (NBC News, Yahoo Finance). The Affiliates Rule part is now settled by a primary source: BIS extended the Affiliates Rule suspension through 2027-01-10 (FR Doc. 2026-22793, filed for public inspection 2026-11-05, published and effective 2026-11-09; src 113, Nixon Peabody src 114). The suspension had run 'until November 9, 2026' under Federal Register 2025-19846 (src 62). The Affiliates Rule binary is therefore 2027-01-10, inside the 12-month horizon; a return then stays in the downside case.
disagreements.evidence: NBC News / Yahoo: US and China agree to extend trade truce through Jan. 10 (Bessent); Federal Register 2025-19846 (src 62); FR Doc. 2026-22793 (src 113); Nixon Peabody 2026-11-06 (src 114).

October customer capex prints, starting with Micron tonight (FY27 capex guide), then Samsung, TSMC and SK hynix. DRAM is ~26-29% of AMAT systems revenue.

China: 28% of revenue. The US-China truce is extended to Jan 10, 2027 (Bessent, Sep 23), The Affiliates Rule suspension runs to Nov 10, 2026 (Yahoo Finance); a report that it is extended with the truce could not be confirmed from a primary source. Either date is a binary event inside the horizon.

The supervisor's thesis break is $335 (~15x a ~$22.8 NTM EPS). Driver restatement: the -20% NTM EPS = WFE -15% vs path (2027-28 digestion), AGS -3% (Affiliates Rule returning: AMAT's 8-K of 2025-10-02 put the FY2026 net revenue effect at approximately $600 million, all segments, src 122), GM -1 pt; multiple -6 turns kept. Update 2026-11-13 (customer-capex build): the WFE -15% delta now applies to non-China foundry/logic capex, non-China memory capex and China Systems alike (cx_fl, cx_mem, ss_cn -15%), i.e. customers cut 2027-28 capex plans 15% against their stated budgets.

drivers.derivation: UPDATE 2026-11-12 (base rolled to FY2026, years FY2027-29): constant 0.528 kept by Kilian's card 2026-11-06 11:36am ET ('Logic + DRAM (-5.8%)'); it is built below from SEMI's July 2026 split (src 2), TSMC's 3Q26 HPC share (src 55) and Micron's FY2026 10-K business-unit mix (src 98, 99). The Q4 FY2026 release (src 116) gives no WFE segment split, TSMC HPC share or Micron mix, so it does not change the inputs.  || EARLIER TEXT (base round, FY2025 base; quarter references are to that layout and superseded where they differ): s = foundry/logic share of WFE x AI (HPC) share of leading-edge foundry + DRAM share of WFE x data-center share of a DRAM maker's revenue = 0.5235 x 0.68 + 0.2845 x 0.606 = 0.3560 + 0.1724 = 0.5284 -> 0.528 (Kilian card 2026-11-06 11:36am ET 'Logic + DRAM (-5.8%)': 'DRAM WFE cut at Micron's 60.6% data-center share'). WFE split: SEMI July 2026 2028 split foundry/logic $104.7B and DRAM $56.9B of ~$200B (src 2) = 0.5235 / 0.2845. HPC share: TSMC 3Q26 'HPC ... represented 68%' of net revenue (src 55). Data-center share: Micron FY2026 10-K (fiscal year ended 2026-09-03), Item 1 products by business unit (src 98): Cloud Memory BU (CMBU) $43.09B + Core Data Center BU (CDBU) $37.59B = $80.68B of the four BUs' $133.17B (MCBU 36.60, AEBU 15.89) = 0.6058 -> 0.606; the four BUs reconcile to reported revenue $133,188M (10-K R3, src 99; $18M rounding). FY2025: 13.52 + 7.23 = 20.75 of 37.36 = 0.555, so the data-center share is rising. Caveats (flagged): 0.606 is Micron's revenue mix including NAND, not DRAM capex or the DC share of DRAM tool demand; SK hynix says demand exceeds supply through 2030 with LTAs over 50% of 2027-28 capacity (src 52), so a pause may delay rather than cancel memory tool orders; 0.68 is TSMC's revenue mix, used for all foundry/logic WFE; NAND and other WFE (~19%) carry no cut. Constant over FY2026-29 at the 2028 split: SEMI's July release gives segment figures for 2026 too (foundry/logic $78.0B, DRAM $38.8B of $143.9B = 0.542 / 0.270, src 2), which give s = 0.542 x 0.68 + 0.270 x 0.606 = 0.532; the 2028 split is used because FY2028 is the year the data-center pause (dc_mor) hits, and the constant only matters where dc_mor is above 0 (Q3 FY27-FY29); the 2026 split would change s by +0.004 (immaterial). The Micron data-center share is rising (0.555 FY2025 -> 0.606 FY2026), so the DRAM factor is not assumed to turn down. Alternatives (former judgment call, decided): logic only s = 0.356; logic + DRAM at the 68% proxy 0.549; all foundry/logic + DRAM 0.808. || UPDATE 2026-11-13: value unchanged; now multiplies non-China Systems (s_fl x cx_fl + s_mem x cx_mem) instead of wfe x shr.
drivers.why: Only the AI/data-center-linked part of WFE is exposed to US data-center pauses; it sets how much of dc_mor reaches Semiconductor Systems revenue.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.question: China Systems FY2027-29: keep +11.8% then flat, or another path?
judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: Update 2026-11-13 (customer-capex build booked, Kilian card 'Customer-capex build'; research target (12m) 448.69 at the 20.43x exit, was 427.45): China Systems revenue was 7,123 in FY2026 (Systems x AMAT's China share of revenue, src 148, 116). Kilian picked '+11.8% then flat' earlier today on a card whose reasoning credited 'China completing its cycle' to the CEO; the citation gate found that is the CFO, talking about the worldwide digestion ending, followed by 'In China, we expect to see that also' (more investment) and AMAT 'gaining share in 2026' in China (src 125). So the flat FY2028-29 has no direct source, and FY2027's +11.8% is FY2026's pace carried one year. What management does say: China grows in 2027 but 'not as fast as those markets that are being pulled by AI', under 25% of the business (src 125); 2027 mature-node growth 'much faster in non-China versus China' (CEO, src 125). Booked, China Systems is ~17% of FY2027 revenue.

options.label: +11.8% in FY27, then flat (booked)
options.reasoning: FY2026's pace for 2027 sits inside the CFO's bounds (growth, below the AI-led non-China +57%, under 25%); flat after because nothing points up past 2027: the CEO's non-China-led ICAPS, SEMI's 'moderate' China growth (src 2) and SEMI's China US$94B over 2026-28, about US$31B a year (src 151). Moderately conservative.

options.label: Flat from FY2027
options.reasoning: SEMI's China 300mm spend of US$94B over 2026-28 (src 151) has no rising path; but it contradicts the CFO's 'We do expect to see growth in China' for 2027 (src 125).

options.label: Half the non-China growth rate
options.reasoning: Reads the CFO's 'not as fast as those markets that are being pulled by AI' (src 125) as China growing at half the non-China Systems rate: +28.7% / +11.0% / +7.0%; the half is a rule of thumb, and FY2027 lands China at ~19% of revenue, still under 25%.

options.label: +11.8% a year through FY29
options.reasoning: The CFO's 'In China, we expect to see that also' (more investment as digestion ends) and share gains in China (src 125) support growth continuing; the rate is FY2026's own (src 148).

options.label: 24% of Systems
options.reasoning: Takes the CFO's 'less than 25% of the business' (src 125) as a level and SEMI's China ~25% of 2026-28 spend (src 151) as the path, so China grows with AI-led non-China capex, which the CFO's 'not as fast' argues against.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.why: Moderately conservative and inside every management statement; the evidence past 2027 is thin, so the lower-growth build is the base.
